title: Britain did pay for the war
notes: Know Your Ally: Britain (US War Department, 1943-44) is an American army film ABOUT Britain: LABEL-AMERICAN-FILM-1944 sits on V4 once, over its first shot (05-01); the narration names it an American army film at P4.08.
One shot per verb on P4.02, cut on the planned word clock (taxed 265.0, borrowed 266.3, directed production 267.7, rationed goods 269.3): re-time the four cuts to the real voice.

Rationed goods is a 1948 ration book (Pop Goes the Weasel): the only legible ration book on disk; Know Your Ally's own rationing shot is a 1.4 s petrol-coupon hand-over (#427, 2282.71-2284.13) that is too short to read. Swap in if a wartime one is preferred.

Plan vs this cut on P4.04: the plan ended on HU49414 (Battersea girls in rubble); that still is scene 07's thesis on 'The celebration does not come with a roof', 90 s later, so it is kept for 07 and this line ends on Pop Goes the Weasel's own bombed street (1948) instead.

P4.05-06: the plan said Keynes still or a Treasury exterior (the reel has none). Keynes still (same static crop as scenes 04 and 13) for 'Keynes worked on the finances', then Pop Goes the Weasel's hand moving coins across an envelope marked PEACE / WAR for 'taxes and deferred pay to hold spending down while production went to war' (a 1948 Treasury film's own device).

Tax captions, the film's own words: EXCESS PROFITS TAX 100% (≈2351-2353.8), LOW INCOME TAX 29% (≈2361-2362.8), HIGH INCOME TAX 97½% (≈2365.5-2370.5). The narrator says no figure. 05-16 overlaps scene 11a's 2365.3-2370.3 (and 13's 2366.0): the same caption comes back later as a deliberate callback; if that is too much, 11a/13 should move, not this first use.
Verb card VERB-1940-PLANT runs the whole of P4.07 (4 s; the plan said 3 s) so no 1 s sliver of picture is left behind it.
P4.11 'organising the peace' is on Pop Goes the Weasel's architect's model of a planned estate (1948), after the plan's VE Day still HU41808 on P4.10.
Credits: Know Your Ally has no exact credit string in footage.md (US War Department, public domain; end credits say 'US National Archives and Records Administration'); left null here.
